banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 22-23, R544: printed pp. 92-93 (pdf 93-94) - the individual area key reaches the demihuman lands: Area 22 the Lands of the Deep Gnomes (the extensive region of long narrow north-south caverns stacked in three levels, averaging 20 by 10 feet, pinching to two or three feet once per mile; the streams never filling the passages and the gnome-built upper walks and spiral stairways; the excavated homes from tiny burrows to crawl-in residences; one clan per cave with its 60-by-8-foot council chamber; the central 200-by-10-foot meeting chamber ringed by the powerful clans; the ~5,000 svirfneblin with a third mobilizable; the protected rothe herds, 100 per clan and eight or 10 times that; the trickling fresh water and still pools; the Grand Canyon air circulation; the edible fungi; the iron-silver-copper-lead mines with five-mile shafts; the smelter and smithy with the coal fires venting to the lava sea; the traded and stockpiled surplus; and the vault - thousands of 500-sp silver bars behind the 550-Strength stone door opened weekly by winch teams and hidden by illusions), and Area 23 the Lower Grand Canyon (the lower portion of Area 7 descending another 1,200 feet; the duergar and deep gnome domains meeting at the canyon, their vast carved galleries of a thousand or more spectators facing each other across the 1,000-foot width; the 20-foot stone bridge; and the arena beneath - a three-dimensional web of stone arches, metal girders, rope ladders and nets where champion duels replace the wars of the past, nonmissile weapons only, the duergar-svirfneblin duels always fatal, the girder spacing hampering the small warriors while humans move easily).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~11935-12079) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (capture idx 212 = the printed p. 93 area-22 tail window and idx 214 head = the area 23 text); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the three levels, the 20/10-ft averages, the once-per-mile 2-3-ft pinches, the 60/8-ft council chambers, the 200/10-ft meeting hall, the 5,000 population with a third mobilizable, the 100-rothe clans with 8-10x herds, the five-mile shafts, the 500-sp silver bars behind the 550-Strength door, the 1,200-ft descent, the thousand-spectator galleries across the 1,000-ft width, and the 20-ft bridge; no cross-read garbles this round - both reads are clean. SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the navigable-boat note lands in Area 24), the Monster Manual denizens (the svirfneblin, duergar, rothe and the Area 7 fauna by reference), the R521-R522 mining (the gnome and duergar mines), and the Area 7 Grand Canyon round itself. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533-R543 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the cavern level count, the width and height averages, the pinch frequency and diameter bounds, the council and meeting chamber dimensions, the population, the rothe minimum and herd multiplier bounds, the mine shaft miles, the vault Strength and the silver bar value, the canyon descent and width and gallery capacity, and the bridge width. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas; no dice appear in this round. The water-travel/MM/mining seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnamCavernLevels
consts.comment: the deep gnomes' caverns are stacked in three distinct levels.

consts.name: dnamCaveWideFt
consts.comment: the deep gnome caves average 20 feet wide.

consts.name: dnamCaveHighFt
consts.comment: the deep gnome caves average 10 feet high.

consts.name: dnamPinchPerMile
consts.comment: at least once each mile travelers encounter a short narrow passage.

consts.name: dnamPinchDiaLoFt
consts.comment: the once-per-mile passage is only two or three feet in diameter (the low bound).

consts.name: dnamPinchDiaHiFt
consts.comment: the once-per-mile passage is two or three feet in diameter (the high bound).

consts.name: dnamCouncilDiaFt
consts.comment: each clan maintains its own council chamber, an excavated chamber about 60 feet in diameter.

consts.name: dnamCouncilHighFt
consts.comment: the clan council chamber is eight feet high.

consts.name: dnamMeetingDiaFt
consts.comment: the clan meeting chamber is a huge chamber 200 feet in diameter.

consts.name: dnamMeetingCeilFt
consts.comment: the meeting chamber ceiling is only 10 feet from the floor, with numerous columns supporting it.

consts.name: dnamSvirfPop
consts.comment: the total population of svirfneblin numbers close to 5,000.

consts.name: dnamRothePerClan
consts.comment: each clan of svirfneblin keeps at least 100 rothe.

consts.name: dnamHerdMultLo
consts.comment: larger rothe herds number eight or 10 times as many beasts as the clan minimum (the low bound).

consts.name: dnamHerdMultHi
consts.comment: larger rothe herds number eight or 10 times the clan minimum (the high bound).

consts.name: dnamMineShaftMiles
consts.comment: many of the deep gnome mine shafts are over five miles long.

consts.name: dnamVaultStr
consts.comment: the vault door requires a combined Strength of 550 to open.

consts.name: dnamSilverBarSp
consts.comment: the vault contains thousands of bars of silver worth 500 sp apiece, alongside the excess products of the smiths.

consts.name: dnamWallsDescendFt
consts.comment: the canyon walls descend another 1,200 feet from this point.

consts.name: dnamGalleryCap
consts.comment: each carved gallery holds a thousand or more spectators.

consts.name: dnamCanyonWideFt
consts.comment: the canyon spans a 1,000-foot width at the bridge.

consts.name: dnamBridgeWideFt
consts.comment: a sturdy stone bridge about 20 feet wide stretches between the two galleries.

bools.name: dnamNorthSouthCaverns
bools.comment: this extensive region of natural caverns comprises numerous long, narrow caverns all running north to south, side by side and also above and below each other.

bools.name: dnamNarrowStretches
bools.comment: in many places the caves become much narrower than their average size.

bools.name: dnamStreamsDryFeet
bools.comment: streams flow through most of the caves but never completely fill the passages; where they come close to choking off tunnels, the svirfneblin have built upper passages so a gnome-sized character can walk anywhere without wet feet.

bools.name: dnamGnomeStairways
bools.comment: the vertical connections between caves are all deep-gnome-crafted small spiral stairways or ladders - tight squeezes for humans, but none too small for them to force through.

bools.name: dnamExcavatedHomes
bools.comment: many small tunnels are excavated in the cave sides as svirfneblin homes, ranging from burrows too small for a human to large multi-family residences or council centers a human could crawl into and stand erect.

bools.name: dnamClanPerCave
bools.comment: each cave in the area is the home of a single clan of the deep gnomes, the most prestigious clans holding the largest caves.

bools.name: dnamMeetingChamber
bools.comment: the gnomes cooperate well and have established a clan meeting chamber in a central cave, surrounded by the residences of the most powerful clans.

bools.name: dnamThirdMobilize
bools.comment: about 1/3 of the svirfneblin population is able to mobilize for military purposes, making them a force to be reckoned with in Deepearth.

bools.name: dnamRotheHerds
bools.comment: many herds of rothe live in the same caverns as the svirfneblin; the gnomes protect them from the more savage predators and use their wooly hair and tasty meat, practicing selective breeding for a healthy livestock supply.

bools.name: dnamTrickleWater
bools.comment: fresh water trickles steadily into the caverns through many small wall and ceiling cracks; no single watercourse is a stream, but the trickles combine to the equivalent of a small stream per cave, gathering in a few large still pools.

bools.name: dnamCanyonAir
bools.comment: the caverns at the southern end of the domain gain air circulation through the Grand Canyon of Deepearth, enough to supply all the caverns amply.

bools.name: dnamEdibleFungi
bools.comment: plant life is represented by the edible fungi that grow throughout the area.

bools.name: dnamGnomeMines
bools.comment: the tunnels branching off the northeast end of the domain are ever-growing mines of iron, silver, copper and lead, extending deep into the earth and horizontally north and east, worked by the industrious gnomes for generations.

bools.name: dnamSmelter
bools.comment: a vast cavern connects the dwellings with the mining tunnels and holds a huge smelter and smithy; massive amounts of coal feed the roaring fires, and exhaust smoke vents through bedrock cracks into the lava sea caverns where it harmlessly disperses.

bools.name: dnamSmithSurplus
bools.comment: svirfneblin blacksmiths, weaponsmiths and armorers toil endlessly creating high-quality weapons, armor and tools - many more than they need; some surplus is traded with other cultures and the rest stockpiled.

bools.name: dnamVaultDoor
bools.comment: a huge stone door blocks off a large vault, sliding along a grooved floor track; the gnomes pull it aside about once a week with a work team of hundreds and a complicated system of winches and pulleys, and a number of illusions conceal the entrance.

bools.name: dnamLowerCanyon
bools.comment: this is the lower portion of the Grand Canyon of Deepearth (Area 7), and the domains of the deep gnomes and the duergar both reach to the canyon itself.

bools.name: dnamBridgedDomains
bools.comment: the canyon is bridged between Areas 22 and 24.

bools.name: dnamCarvedGalleries
bools.comment: on each side of the canyon the demi-humans have carved vast galleries capable of holding a thousand or more spectators, facing each other across the canyon.

bools.name: dnamArenaWeb
bools.comment: below the bridge, in full view of both galleries, is a three-dimensional web of stone arches, metal girders, rope ladders and nets - an arena of subterranean competition.

bools.name: dnamArea7Denizens
bools.comment: denizens and resources are as explained under Area 7, noting that svirfneblin and duergar war parties constantly watch each other across the canyon.

bools.name: dnamChampionDuels
bools.comment: the arena is a treacherous structure upon which most conflicts among the duergar and deep gnomes (and interracial fights) are resolved: the tragic costly wars of the past convinced the demi-humans to appoint a champion per faction and have them fight to the death rather than risk the devastation of war.

bools.name: dnamNonmissileArms
bools.comment: the champions carry an assortment of nonmissile weapons onto the girders and fight to the death; the conflict may sometimes resolve sooner, but a duergar-svirfneblin duel always results in a fatality.

bools.name: dnamArenaManeuver
bools.comment: the three-dimensional arena allows a unique combat in which opponents maneuver for height, positions of security and openings for attack; the girders and beams are spaced far enough apart that the small warriors often have difficulty reaching each other, while humans and larger creatures move through more easily.
